- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2069b81c266836fd6d7b52fc5e6679c734bdcd3c` → `packageMentionDocs`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `488c2fe49d4fbb2786a141e2628bc6e99ffbf402`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/external-binding-datasource.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/refused-shapes.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.object-external-binding-managed-datasource-refused.ts + docs/adr/0015-external-datasource-federation.md, packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/apply.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/federated-object.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/system/datasources/showcase-external.datasource.ts, .changeset/25168-external-binding-managed-datasource-refused.md, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, packages/spec/src/data/external-binding-datasource.test.ts, packages/spec/src/stack-external-binding-datasource.test.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/refused-shapes.test.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object-strictness-batch20.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.external-binding-primary-datasource-refusal.test.ts

Inputs: card #25168 (body, triage 6333828054, claim 6335118058, dev report 6339972223), PR #25192 (body, 12 files, the diff against main), and the 42 check-runs on this head: 35 success, 7 skipped by path selection (18.x upgrade harness, Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance), 0 failed, 0 pending. Those conclusions are the gate verdicts here: Check Changeset (the job that runs `check-adr-0087-registration`), Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Test Core 1/6 to 6/6 and the aggregate, Type Check · workspace, TypeScript Type Check, Build Core, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate (aggregate success; its three shards path-skipped, so the dev's local battery is the dogfood reading and is not re-run here), and the three card/branch guards — all success. Nothing built, run or re-run locally; committed blobs read with `git show` after a fetch.

Face: schema — the five `packages/spec/src/**` hits decide it. The `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line is also present, at the start of a line in the PR body and in the changeset, and reads as a declared narrowing; that face maps to the same tier, so `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` stands on either reading.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`ObjectSchema`'s accept set narrows — RIGHT.** An object carrying `external` (an empty binding included) whose `datasource` is omitted or `'default'` is refused at `['external']`, code `custom`, by `refuseExternalBindingOnPrimaryDatasource` inside the existing `.superRefine` of `object.zod.ts`. The parsed `datasource` is `.optional().default('default')` (object.zod.ts:2625) and the predicate reads a missing or empty string as the primary too, so the parsed and the stored readings agree. `'default'` is managed by construction: stack.zod.ts:548 refuses a stack datasource of that name as host-reserved, so no artefact can re-declare it external, and ADR-0015 §1 makes federation a property of the datasource. Every object door inherits the refusal with no second check: `ObjectSchema.create` (throws at module load — pinned), `defineStack` (`STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` 422 at `objects.N.external` — pinned), `os validate` (`loadConfig` loads the default export, which is `defineStack`'s result), the object save door (kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts:91 maps `object` to `ObjectSchema`; `422 INVALID_METADATA`, the issue at `external`, nothing stored — pinned in the metadata-protocol test), and the stored-row load, which registers the row anyway under `[metadata_spec_invalid]` (protocol.ts:31601, objectql registry.ts:5124), so metadata at rest keeps loading exactly as the changeset's "Unchanged" bullet says.

2. **`defineStack`'s accept set narrows — RIGHT.** `collectExternalBindingDatasourceErrors` runs inside `validateCrossReferences` on `result.data`, the strict parse's output (stack.zod.ts:5088), so a declared datasource's `schemaMode` already carries the spec default `'managed'` (datasource.zod.ts:673) and the `mode` / `schema_mode` aliases are already folded. An object naming a datasource this stack declares with `schemaMode: 'managed'` or none → `STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID` 422, one finding per bound object; `'external'` and `'validate-only'` accepted; an undeclared name gets no verdict (absence of a definition is not evidence about its `schemaMode`, and the host's and other packages' datasources are not visible); `strict: false` returns before the parse and the pass, by the existing contract. The primary half never reaches this pass and `'default'` cannot be in the declared map, so no object is found twice. Placement after the `objectNames.size === 0` return is right: no objects, no bindings. `os validate` and `os build` inherit it through `defineStack`.

3. **What stays accepted — RIGHT, and stated in every carrier.** A binding on a datasource the door cannot see: the save door with a named stored datasource (`wh`, managed or unset) still saves; a stack naming an undeclared datasource still passes; and the `composeStacks` artifact pass, whose step 3b re-runs two artifact-scoped rules only, never pairs an external object of one input with a managed datasource another input declares. The PR body's table (row 4), its Acceptance notes, the changeset's "Unchanged" bullet, the entry's `reason`, the predicate's docblock and the save-door test's header all say so. Judged in ③.

4. **"A package `defaultDatasource` or a `datasourceMapping` rule does not count" — RIGHT.** `assertWriteAllowed` (objectql/src/engine.ts:9702) reads `object.datasource`, returns on `'default'` and on a datasource with no or `'managed'` `schemaMode`; `isFederatedObject` (federated-object.ts:33) is a presence test on `external`. An object routed only by a mapping is exactly the split the card describes, so the binding has to be on the object's own `datasource`, and the refusal message says so.

5. **ADR-0087 kit — RIGHT.** The D3 entry `18.object-external-binding-managed-datasource-refused.ts` has the `SemanticMigration` shape of its siblings (id, surface, replacement, reason, acceptanceCriteria); no `conversionIds`, right for a refusal nothing rewrites losslessly; `relevantWhen` omitted, which the type allows — the entry is then always listed by `os migrate meta`, a noise cost only. The directory listing is the registry (`gen:migration-registry`). The `REFUSED_STORED_SHAPES` detector carries the same id and `toMajor: 18`, lists one TODO per refused object with `from` and a reason naming the owner's three choices, runs on the converted stack (conversions/apply.ts:188), and the registration test enumerates it. Listing-only note: the detector reads a stored datasource row's `schemaMode` key raw, so a stored row written under the `mode` / `schema_mode` alias would list as managed — a TODO, never a refusal; the parse's own verdict is unaffected.

6. **Public surface — RIGHT.** `externalBindingDatasourceRefusal` is not re-exported from `data/index.ts` (no api-surface row; Lint & Repo Gates green). `ObjectExtensionSchema` (object.zod.ts:4018) exposes no `external` key, so an extension cannot add a binding past the refinement. The `.describe()` strings of `external` are unchanged, so the generated JSON Schema and references are unmoved (the dev's `check:generated` 14/14 reading, Lint green). No consumer package changes source; the engine-double ledger and one test are the only non-spec files.

7. **Fixtures — RIGHT.** The four batch-20 fixtures now name `remote_crm` (undeclared → no verdict), so their unknown-key assertions still pin what they pinned. The 62 runtime fixtures that hand `external` without `datasource` straight to drivers, the engine or lint bypass the parse and model what a legacy stored row still reaches; green on this head; answered in ③.

8. **Producers (the stop condition) — RIGHT.** Read on the head tree: the only object with `external` outside tests is the showcase's, bound to `showcase_external`, declared `schemaMode: 'external'` (showcase-external.datasource.ts); every other `remoteName` hit is a driver or CLI struct field, not object metadata; the CLI zoo fixture names its federated datasource. HotCRM (0 producers) is the dev's reading, not re-read here. No conversion question applies.

9. **Remainder (the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`):** `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`, three rows for the new test's engine double, a mechanical `--write` output named in the PR body.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/25168-external-binding-managed-datasource-refused.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor` — RIGHT. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is the kind (a value refused: `external` on the primary or on a managed declared datasource), a kind takes at least `minor` on the package the diff moves, and `(narrowing)` is BREAKING: the body carries the banner, FROM, TO in its three arms, the unchanged set and the one-line fix (`datasource: 'warehouse'` beside a `schemaMode: 'external'` declaration). `minor` rather than `major` is the launch-window convention the changeset names.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — TRUE, line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset, the exact spelling the fleet's reader keys on. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` — TRUE in both.
- ADR-0087 disposition: exactly one marker, `adr-0087: registered object-external-binding-managed-datasource-refused`, naming the D3 entry this same diff adds (the gate's resolve-at-HEAD and added-by-this-diff facts); Check Changeset success.
- No changeset is owed by `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: its door changes behaviour through the spec dependency alone; the diff adds it a test and no source. `skip-changeset` is not claimed; `content/docs/releases` is untouched.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations (six), each answered:
1. Branch `claude/project-thread-5h4pzn`, not an `issue-25168` slug — the claim names it and "The card this PR closes must claim this branch" is success. Accepted.
2. First ablation attempt killed mid-build with an EXIT-only trap — the restore is proven on the committed bytes: the diff's index line for `external-binding-datasource.ts` is blob `8a978cd3`, the hash the dev compared to HEAD, and the three gates overlapping the window were rerun. Accepted as a process note; the head is what CI judged.
3. First dogfood run interrupted, rerun in full on this head — accepted as the dev's reading; the CI shards are path-skipped and nothing is re-run here.
4. `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` outside the claimed surface — a mechanical ledger for the new test's double, named in the PR body, with the precedent the dev cites; the lane seat's remainder. Accepted.
5. Tests narrowed from message wording to code, status, path and the subject-naming first sentence — right under the os-dev rule; the anchors still pin which object and which datasource is refused.
6. Worktree kept for the review round — procedural; accepted.

The open question (dev report 6339972223: the object save door cannot see a named datasource's `schemaMode`; a stored `wh`, managed or unset, plus an object binding it with `external` still saves; A a follow-up card, B leave it; recommendation A):
- **Is the PR's claim of what it enforces honest about the gap? YES.** The gap is declared in the PR body's table and Acceptance notes ("still saves, measured on this head"), in the changeset's "Unchanged" bullet, in the entry's `reason`, in the predicate's docblock and in the save-door test's header. The PR claims the parse half and the same-stack half, and only those.
- **Does the gap block this PR? NO — it belongs to a follow-up card (A), which the seat files before this PR lands and links from the PR body.** The route (triage 6333828054) put the rule at the parse, inherited by the save door, with no second check in objectql, and the claim's surface is `packages/spec/src/**` with stop-on-breach. Closing the named-datasource half at the save door needs a datasource lookup inside `saveMetaItem` (metadata-protocol) and the predicate exported (an api-surface row): a different door and a different surface. No producer was measured (0 in the repo, 0 in HotCRM), and the gap is loud. Against the card's "done" (every authoring and load door refuses), this PR closes the measured defect (`defineStack`), both NOT-MEASURED readings for the primary, and leaves one authoring half open and named — `Fixes #25168` stands on the triage route, with the remainder on its own card. That card should carry, on the same predicate: (a) the object save door resolving the object's datasource (stored row or registry definition) and refusing 422 at `external`; (b) the reverse direction, a datasource saved or changed to managed while stored objects bind it with `external`; (c) the `composeStacks` artifact pass, which today does not re-run `validateCrossReferences` across inputs (read at step 3b) — the one load door that can see both halves across packages. Option B is wrong: it keeps the split runtime answer the card was filed on.

Out-of-scope findings (four): items 1 to 3 are the follow-up card above, which gives them the carrier the report left blank. Item 4 (`content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx` §5 shows `ObjectSchema.create` with `external` and no `datasource`, a shape that now throws at module load) is a docs-only touch-up, not governed, non-blocking; the seat files or folds it.

Acceptance note, 62 runtime fixtures not rewritten — accepted: they bypass the parse and test what a legacy stored row still reaches (it registers under `[metadata_spec_invalid]`); green on this head. They now describe a shape the contract refuses, so a later sweep may re-home them under a stored-row harness; not this PR's.

Escalated, not blocking:
- **ADR-0015 §4.2's mechanism sentence is now imprecise.** The record says the invariant is "enforced at metadata-load time, not in the Zod schema, because the datasource may live in another artefact". This PR keeps the half that needs the other artefact out of the Zod schema (`defineStack`'s cross-reference pass) and puts the self-contained half, the primary, into `ObjectSchema`'s refinement: the ADR's reason is honoured and its decision, the invariant, is implemented, not reversed, so Prime Directive #13 is not engaged. `docs/adr/**` is Tier H and rightly untouched here; the maintainer amends §4.2's sentence by hand (judged at the parse for `'default'`, at `defineStack` for a declared datasource, and at the save door for a stored one once the follow-up lands). The `object.zod.ts` docblocks already describe the split.
- Triage's protocol note — `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is "reported to the maintainer in this round's record" — is the seat's round record to carry, together with the ADR amendment above.
- No `scripts/adr-anchors/` entry anchors `external-binding-datasource.ts` to ADR-0015; the file cites the ADR and its section in its docblock, and the anchor README makes one optional. Note only.
